List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Nipun Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ashish Kumar Gaur, learned counsel for the informant and Sri V.K. Gupta, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Sessions Trial No.217 of 2019 arising out of Case Crime No.493 of 2018, registered under Sections 498A, 323, 313,
504, 506, 376 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act at Police Station- Puranpur, District Pilibhit with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. As per prosecution story, the applicant, who happens to be the brother-in-law of the informant, is stated to have attempted to rape her in addition to several other allegations of demand of dowry and Ashish Tripathi vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The present FIR is a counterblast to the divorce petition filed by the brother of the applicant Anshul Tripathi on 23.07.2018.
The present FIR has been instituted on 11.08.2018.

The said FIR and the petition filed under Section 125 Cr.P.C. indicate the allegation that an attempt to rape her has been made by the applicant, but in the statement of the victim recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C., she has levelled the allegations of committing rape with her on 18.03.2019.
The said statement has been taken after legal consultation after much delay.
6. Learned counsel has further stated that the case of the applicant is at a different footing to the husband Anshul Tripathi.
The applicant has simply been implicated owing to his relationship with Anshul Tripathi.
The main accused person Anshul Tripathi resides at Mumbai and does a job there.
The victim and her husband used to live there.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application on the ground that the applicant has availed all the opportunities available to him and had even failed in a petition field u/s 482 Cr.P.C., but could not dispute the said facts as narrated by the counsel for the applicant.

8. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., taking into consideration the fact that the allegations per se against the applicant have been inflated during her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. and the case of the applicants stands at a different footing to the main accused person Anshul Tripathi, and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
9. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.

11. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously as early as possible in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgments of the Apex Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
